ONGOING STORYLINES:
- Copper surplus vs. scarcity (logged Oct 16): ICSG projects the global surplus to more than triple by 2027. Copper fell for a third day on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk. Anglo American's CEO says tech giants are circling amid copper scarcity. Antofagasta shares fell on a flat 2027 copper outlook.
- Copper project plans (logged Oct 16): CoTec and BMR plan a partnership to boost Punitaqui copper output (Yahoo Finance). An Austrian investor is rushing to boost output at an old Chile mine (Reuters). Codelco and Normet partner on autonomous underground mining (Global Mining Review). No tonnages or dates given in any of these.
- Vale cost pressure (logged Oct 16): Vale says soaring costs put 10% of its iron ore in the red (Mining.com, repeated in feed, logged once). No price benchmark, period, or cost basis given. Pimenta on Vale's emerging copper story (International Mining).
- Miner economics (logged Oct 16): Crux Investor argues royalty holders and fuel-hedged miners fare better as costs rise (investor commentary, not data).
- Canadian mining tax credit (logged Oct 16): Nearly half of provinces and territories ask Ottawa to expand the mining tax credit (constructconnect.com). No instrument, rate, or cap specified.
- Chile miner deaths (logged Oct 16): WSWS reports seven miners dead in three weeks. Source is partisan; figure unconfirmed.
- Gold M&A (logged Oct 16): Breakingviews says Gold Fields' $27bn play may stay in the M&A pit. Equinox's output rose 34% after its Orla merger. Gold Fields–Equinox entry was unsourced and not logged today.
- Hycroft (logged Oct 16): MINING.COM reports "bonanza" gold grades at its Nevada mine. No assay data or technical report yet. Assay entry was unsourced and not logged today.
- Lithium (logged Oct 16): PLS approved a $1.3bn Pilgangoora expansion. Pantera announced a US$2bn EnergyX lithium supply agreement. Pantera entry was unsourced and not logged today.
- LM Baraga Basin (logged Oct 16): US Department of War is investing $5.22m in the project. LM entry was unsourced and not logged today.
- Deep-sea mining order (logged Oct 16): Foley Hoag reviewed the legal landscape since the 2025 executive order. Legal status disputed.

THE DESK'S EVOLVING VIEWS:
- Meldrum (Oct 16): Treats the copper surplus as near-term fact and scarcity as a longer bet visible in M&A. Reads Breakingviews as signalling more bidding rounds. Cannot confirm the deep-sea legal picture without the Foley Hoag piece. Disagrees with Yukon on copper timing and gold M&A. Oct 16: says do not net copper project plans against the 2027 surplus yet; sees Codelco–Normet as a concentrate and lead-time signal; says Vale's cost cause matters, since cost inflation and a falling benchmark lead to different outcomes.
- Yukon Cornelius (Oct 16): Surplus forecasts describe refined metal, while scarcity talk concerns concentrate, grades, and lead times, so both can hold. Calls the Breakingviews piece commentary, not a deal. Sees Equinox's output jump as acquired, not organic. Describes the deep-sea order as legally unsettled. Rates Pantera medium confidence. Oct 16: agrees on no netting; says autonomy mainly changes cost per tonne, not annual output (disagrees with Meldrum); says high-cost tonnes go uneconomic first; says royalties, paid on revenue, are sturdier than the Crux ranking suggests.
- Dr I Simon (Oct 16): Sees copper's apparent contradiction as mostly a measurement problem. Flags US tariff policy as a live risk, with no COMEX or LME series in the material. Keeps unverified claims out of conclusions. Rates Pantera low confidence. Oct 16: treats the Vale figure as one unexplained data point, with no consolidation or distress call; says copper items neither confirm nor weaken the refined surplus view, and surplus plus tight concentrate supply can coexist; says the royalty-on-revenue argument stands alone and needs contract checks; says the tax-credit prediction may test the wrong instrument until the submission is read.
- Change of mind, Simon (Oct 16): Withdrew the lower-bond-yields explanation for gold. It is now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test.
- No changes of mind recorded on Oct 16 for copper or Vale.
